extraction.name: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
extraction.description: A paper describing a fully automated pipeline to collect real-world interactive software engineering tasks from GitHub repositories, build the SWE-rebench dataset, and create a decontaminated benchmark for evaluating software engineering agents.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by an automated pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive SWE tasks from GitHub repositories. The process downloads raw input data from GitHub Archive and GitHub, links issues with pull requests, filters candidates using several criteria, automatically generates installation instructions, verifies execution in containers, and assesses task quality using an LLM fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly notes that the git tag command provides a version for approximately 95% of task instances, and unique versions are assigned to the rest. It also notes that some repositories lack successful installation recipes or have flaky tests, unpinned dependencies, or incomplete/unsuitable tasks that are filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw input data came from GitHub Archive public event JSON archives and cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories. The pipeline also used issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata such as creation dates and labels, and repository files such as README.md, Dockerfile, setup.py, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, and environment.yml.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025 were used for initial dataset building; the benchmark analysis includes tasks created in January 2025 and March-April 2025.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No explicit imputation protocol is described.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Issues and pull requests were linked when PR titles or descriptions mentioned resolving the issue. The overall patch was split into solution patch and test patch. Versions were normalized to major.minor format. For verification, exact dependency versions were frozen using pip freeze and conda env export after successful setup.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering required the issue to be from a Python repository with a permissive license, marked resolved, linked to a merged PR on the main branch, not linked to multiple issues, have an issue description longer than 10 characters, introduce or modify tests, include code changes beyond test files, and affect 1 to 15 files. Tasks were then grouped by project version, installed in containers, and retained only if execution-based verification passed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotations from SWE-bench Verified were used to fine-tune an instruction-following model to predict Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness. The resulting LLM-generated labels were attached as metadata to each task instance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For each of over 3,800 examples, the model was trained to predict each label independently using a 75/25 train/validation split. The paper reports validation performance for each label and notes that the automated assessment is not perfect but useful for filtering and task selection.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct was used for installation recipe generation and for task quality assessment after fine-tuning; TractoAI was used for distributed execution; buildah was used for container installation; pip freeze and conda env export were used to record dependency versions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The SWE-rebench leaderboard is continuously updated with fresh tasks. The paper states that the current set of evaluated models can be found on the leaderboard website and that the benchmark is maintained as a continuously updated, decontaminated evaluation resource.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No explicit collection of personal sensitive information is described. The dataset includes repository and issue metadata, but no human demographic attributes are reported as collected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the benchmark may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering and could contribute to overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse for introducing vulnerabilities. It argues that openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking help mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited exclusively to Python in its initial release, and the benchmark subset is filtered to English issues, low-to-moderate difficulty, clean test execution, and tasks with at most 3 modified files and 50 fail-to-pass tests. The paper also discusses potential contamination bias in existing benchmarks and notes that automated quality assessment may introduce errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may produce imperfectly described or unsolvable tasks and cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment. The initial release is limited to Python, and adapting the pipeline to other languages requires language-specific components. Automated installation recipe generation was validated on only 18 repositories and may miss project subtleties.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, reinforcement learning, benchmarking, validation, and fine-tuning of software engineering agents. The benchmark is used for standardized evaluation of LLM-based agents, with decontaminated tasks and repeated runs for pass@k-style assessment.
